title: Token Usage Harmonization: Consensus-merge Pipeline for Billing Attribution
creator: Marco Liu
description: Problem: We observe persistent small divergences between token counts surfaced by streaming collectors, batch aggregators, and the billing exporter. These deltas cause customer confusion and occasional invoice adjustments. Goal: implement a 'consensus-merge' pipeline that ingests multiple token sources, applies deterministic fingerprinting and event-time joins, and emits a single canonical token usage record per request/session for downstream billing and console analytics. Scope: - Sources: streaming-token-collector, final-aggregates (daily batch), sdk-side counters, and webhook-derived usage. - Output: canonical_token_usage (per-tenant, per-route, per-model, per-request-id) plus per-tenant reconciliation report and an adjustments queue for billing reconciler. - Constraints: maintain eventual consistency, support retroactive corrections within invoice window, avoid double-billing, and scale to peak throughput (est. 12k req/s).
comments: 2026-02-11 - Marco Liu: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to do event-time join with 2-hour watermark, prefer idempotent fingerprints based on (tenant, request_id, model, timestamp_bucket). Action: prototype streaming join in Flink/Beam and compare to existing batch aggregates.

2026-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Design doc uploaded with two architecture options: (A) append-only consensus stream with conflict-resolution rule (max-token-count) and (B) weighted merge using source-confidence scores. We decided to prototype A first for deterministic behavior.

2026-02-25 - Priya Kapoor (Data Eng review): Suggested dedupe window + tombstone handling for late-arriving sdk counters. Raised concern about memory pressure for long-lived session keys; recommended sharding by tenant and TTL-based index.
